subject: Entitlement rebalance + proposed capacity upgrade (Q3 term change)
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skywardai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@skywardai.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:11:00 -0700
Subject: Quick sync: May overages + Q3 ramp

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the call earlier. FYI we pulled the May token export and saw a much higher inference rate than anticipated after we turned on the new personalization pipeline. Attached is a CSV with a breakdown by model/route.

Immediate ask: can Redwood propose a short-term entitlement adjustment and a recommended capacity uplift for Q3? We have budget flexibility if we can avoid sustained overage charges. Also cc'ing finance so they can flag any procurement constraints.

High-level:
- Current committed tokens: 1.2B/year
- May actual (projected run-rate): ~2.4B/year if sustained
- Peak latency still within SLOs but cost per 1k tokens up ~18% due to longer context windows

Could Naomi or someone on ops send a recommended sizing + two pricing options (conservative and aggressive)? We'd like to move quickly — deadline for finance sign-off is next Friday.

Thanks,
Alex
Product Ops | Skyward AI
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skywardai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, finance@skywardai.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync: May overages + Q3 ramp

Alex —

Appreciate the data. I ran a quick pass with our Optimize tooling and attached a token report (CSV) plus a proposed term matrix. High-level recommendations below; full details in the attachments.

Recommended short-term path (Option A — conservative):
- Add a 750M token true-up for the remainder of the contract year (pro-rated), no change to per-token price.
- Create a temporary burst pool (Dedicated) that covers 30% of peak with autoscaling enabled; this avoids overage billing while we onboard quantization profiles.

Recommended expansion path (Option B — aggressive):
- Move to a 2.5B committed tier for 12 months with a 9% unit discount and a 60-day exit window for capacity reduction.
- Include two automated cache rules for large prefix reuse to lower effective token spend by 10-15% in steady state.

Operational notes:
- Latency profile looks stable — no change to SLOs expected with burst pool.
- We recommend a short A/B rollout of the quantized variant on 10% of traffic to validate quality impact (ops can coordinate).

Marissa — please weigh in on the rollout support and customer success timeline. Ben — if pricing looks ok, can you draft the amendment language?

Naomi
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync: May overages + Q3 ramp

Thanks Naomi — I can own the customer rollout. Timeline proposal:
- Wed Jun 16: Ship quantized-variant canary (10% traffic) + monitoring dashboard (latency/cost/quality).
- Fri Jun 18: Review canary quality with Alex; if no regression proceed to 50% over 72 hours.
- Mon Jun 21: Full rollout and final entitlements applied.

I'll prepare a short runbook and a success checklist for Skyward's engineers. Priyom, can infra reserve the burst pool and confirm autoscale thresholds?

-M
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skywardai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed term amendment and pricing options

Alex —

Following Naomi's recommendations, attached is a short amendment with two rows (Option A conservative true-up, Option B 12-month uplift + discount). Quick notes:
- Option A removes any overage for the pro-rated true-up period; one-time invoice for the 750M tokens.
- Option B requires a 12-month minimum commitment; includes a 9% discount and a single mid-term entitlement rebalancing allowance (up to 20% of committed tokens).

If it helps, I'm happy to hop on a 30-minute alignment call with finance this Thursday.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skywardai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@skywardai.com, Lydia Park <lydia.park@skywardai.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed term amendment and pricing options

Thanks all — the options look straightforward. Finance prefers Option B if we can get a 60-day reduction clause (you mentioned 60-day exit — can you confirm how that applies?) and a mid-term rebalancing allowance that avoids a full renegotiation.

Lydia (finance) — are you available Thursday 10:30 PT for Ben to walk through numbers?

Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skywardai.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed term amendment and pricing options

Alex, Lydia —

Confirming: Option B includes a 12-month committed term at 2.5B tokens with a 9% unit discount. The 60-day reduction clause allows Skyward to reduce committed capacity once during the 12-month term with 60 days' notice; the reduction is capped at 25% of committed tokens and triggers a pro-rated pricing reconciliation. Mid-term rebalancing (up to 20% of committed tokens) is allowed twice and does not require renegotiation.

I've updated the amendment draft (amendment_draft_skyward_v2.pdf) to reflect this language. If this satisfies finance, I'll send the DocuSign link for signature after today's alignment call.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
